# Recording format

Each episode is recorded as one MCAP file, `recording.mcap` in its
folder. It carries everything it was recorded with, so it can be
understood without Kapto or the files beside it: tools such as
`mcap info` and Foxglove show its records as they are.

## Channels

One channel per stream, named after it. Each message is the payload
exactly as received, its log time the receive time mapped to UTC, and
its publish time the time its source gave it, as the source has it:
for a ROS 2 topic, its publisher's timestamp, as rosbag2 writes it.
Without one, the publish time is the log time. A
stream with a layout has it as its channel's schema ([Struct
layout](struct-layout.md), [Layouts by path](path-layout.md)).
A stream of ROS 2 messages is stored as rosbag2 stores a topic, so
ROS 2's tools read it: message encoding `cdr`, and a schema
of encoding `ros2msg` named after the message type (e.g.
`sensor_msgs/msg/JointState`) whose data is its definition as rosbag2
writes it; the fields Kapto decodes go in the channel's metadata under
`kapto.fields`, as a JSON stream's schema holds them. Other
streams have message encoding `kapto.raw` and no schema.

### Events: `kapto.events`

Every recording has one channel of Kapto's own, `kapto.events`: what
happened while it was recorded, at a moment or over a stretch. An episode
started or ended, a stream lost messages, an action began or ended, an
operator noted something. Each message is one event as JSON (message
encoding `json`, schema encoding `jsonschema`), its log time the event's
moment on the same clock as the streams' messages, so it lines up with
what the robot sent. Events are written between the streams' batches, so
an event can come a little after messages received later than it in the
file: order them by their moment. A stream's ID never holds a dot, so no
stream is named like a channel of Kapto's own (`kapto.…`).

- `kind`: what happened, lowercase words joined by dots (`grasp`,
`subtask.reach`); kinds beginning `kapto.` are Kapto's own.
- `phase`: `moment` (left out), or `begin` and `end` of a stretch, paired
by the same `kind` and `id` and sent as each happens, or `stretch`, a
whole stretch told at once, from `at_utc_ns` to `until_utc_ns`.
- `source`: `kapto`, `page`, `api`, `cli` or `robot:<stream>`.
- `text` and `attributes`: what someone said about it, if anything.

Kapto keeps these of its own during an episode, from source `kapto`,
saying when in it a stream had trouble, which its totals don't:

| Kind | When | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| `kapto.stream_lost` | A stream lost messages, at most once a second | `stream`, `lost_upstream`, `dropped_by_us`: how many since the last |
| `kapto.stream_silent` | A stream sent nothing for 2 s | `stream` |
| `kapto.stream_back` | A silent stream sent again | `stream` |

Fields are only ever added, like every output format.

```json
{
  "kind": "grasp",
  "at_utc_ns": 1772700412500000000,
  "phase": "begin",
  "id": "g1",
  "source": "page",
  "text": "second try",
  "attributes": {
    "hand": "left"
  }
}
```

The channel's schema:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "Event",
  "description": "Something that happened at a moment, or the beginning or end of a\nstretch in which something happened.",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "at_utc_ns": {
      "description": "When, in UTC nanoseconds, on the same clock as the messages'\nreceive times; for a whole stretch, when it began.",
      "type": "integer",
      "format": "int64"
    },
    "attributes": {
      "description": "More about it, as names and texts.",
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "id": {
      "description": "Pairs a beginning with its end: the same kind and ID. Required for\nboth.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "kind": {
      "description": "What happened: dotted lowercase words, e.g. `grasp` or\n`kapto.stream_lost`. Kinds beginning `kapto.` are Kapto's own.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "phase": {
      "description": "Whether it is a moment, the beginning or end of a stretch, or a\nwhole stretch.",
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Phase",
      "default": "moment"
    },
    "source": {
      "description": "Where it came from: `kapto`, `page`, `api`, `cli`, or `robot:<stream>`.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "text": {
      "description": "What someone said about it, if anything.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "until_utc_ns": {
      "description": "When a whole stretch ended, on the same clock; only for one.",
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ],
      "format": "int64"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "kind",
    "at_utc_ns",
    "source"
  ],
  "$defs": {
    "Phase": {
      "description": "Whether an event is a moment or one end of a stretch.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "description": "It happened at that moment.",
          "type": "string",
          "const": "moment"
        },
        {
          "description": "A stretch began.",
          "type": "string",
          "const": "begin"
        },
        {
          "description": "A stretch ended.",
          "type": "string",
          "const": "end"
        },
        {
          "description": "A whole stretch, from `at_utc_ns` to `until_utc_ns`, told at once,\ne.g. when it is marked afterwards.",
          "type": "string",
          "const": "stretch"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Metadata records

A record maps names to texts: nested fields have dotted names,
numbers and switches are written as text, lists as JSON, and absent
fields are left out. Records are only ever added to, like every
output format.

### `kapto.episode`

Written when recording starts, before the first message, so a
recording cut off part-way still says what it is. The same values as
[`episode.json`](episode.md), under the same names: the episode's ID,
the Kapto version that recorded it, when it started, the robot
package (absent for an `unchecked` episode), and the copies of the
session profile and task, each with its hash (absent when none was
chosen).

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| `id` | `20260305T192345.123Z-1a2b3c4d` |
| `kapto_version` | `0.1.0` |
| `package.hash` | `9f2c…` |
| `package.id` | `arm7` |
| `package.version` | `0.1.0` |
| `profile.environment` | `lab 2, bench A` |
| `profile.hash` | `4e1a…` |
| `profile.id` | `lab_ana` |
| `profile.mode` | `teleoperated` |
| `profile.operator` | `Ana` |
| `profile.tags` | `["shift-a"]` |
| `started_utc_ns` | `1772700400000000000` |
| `task.hash` | `b07d…` |
| `task.id` | `pick_and_place` |
| `task.name` | `Pick and place` |
| `task.objects` | `["red cube","bin"]` |
| `task.prompt` | `Pick up the red cube and put it in the bin` |
| `task.subtasks` | `["reach","grasp"]` |

### `kapto.capture`

Written when recording starts: the settings that shaped the
recording. `writer.*` is how it is written: compression, chunk size,
and how often it is put on disk. `buffers.<thread>.*` is each input's
buffers, named after the thread that receives it. `attach_meshes` is
whether it carries the package's meshes (`capture.attach_meshes`), and
`left_out.<path>` the SHA-256 of each package file it doesn't (see
below), so it can be matched to a package later. Never a secret.

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| `attach_meshes` | `false` |
| `buffers.cap-rx-udp-0.batch_capacity` | `256` |
| `buffers.cap-rx-udp-0.batches` | `252` |
| `buffers.cap-rx-udp-0.max_message_len` | `1500` |
| `buffers.cap-rx-udp-0.memory_bytes` | `96768000` |
| `left_out.meshes/link_1.stl` | `5b0e…` |
| `writer.chunk_bytes` | `1048576` |
| `writer.compression` | `lz4` |
| `writer.compression_level` | `0` |
| `writer.sync_interval_ns` | `500000000` |

### `kapto.summary`

Written when recording ends, before the file is closed, so a recording
without it wasn't finished. The same values as `episode.json` then:
when it ended, how the host's clock behaved (`clock.*`), how close the
buffers came to full (`buffers.*`), and every stream's counts under its
name (`streams.<stream>.*`). How long messages waited to be on disk is
only in `episode.json`: it includes putting the closed file on disk.

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| `buffers.batches` | `6` |
| `buffers.memory_bytes` | `2304000` |
| `buffers.peak_batches` | `2` |
| `clock.max_uncertainty_ns` | `250000` |
| `clock.samples` | `1` |
| `clock.steps` | `[]` |
| `ended_utc_ns` | `1772700460000000000` |
| `streams.arm_joints.decoded` | `120000` |
| `streams.arm_joints.dropped_by_us` | `0` |
| `streams.arm_joints.loss_detection` | `sequence` |
| `streams.arm_joints.lost_upstream` | `2` |
| `streams.arm_joints.received` | `120000` |
| `streams.arm_joints.written` | `120000` |
| `streams.tf_static.carried` | `2` |
| `streams.tf_static.decoded` | `0` |
| `streams.tf_static.dropped_by_us` | `0` |
| `streams.tf_static.loss_detection` | `undetectable` |
| `streams.tf_static.lost_upstream` | `0` |
| `streams.tf_static.received` | `0` |
| `streams.tf_static.written` | `0` |

### `kapto.carried`

Written when recording starts, after `kapto.capture` and the
attachments, if the episode starts with messages kept from before it. A stream whose
messages are kept for late subscribers (a ROS 2 topic subscribed to
with `durability = "transient_local"`, such as `/tf_static`) may
send them once, long before an episode: capture keeps the newest
(as many as the subscription's `depth`) and starts every episode
with them, as that stream's first messages. Each is written as
received, with its publish time, but at the episode's start as its
log time, so the episode plays from its start; when it was received
is here, under its stream's name: a JSON list of receive times in UTC
nanoseconds, in the order written.

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| `tf_static` | `[1772699800000000000,1772699800002000000]` |

### `kapto.clock_map`

Written when recording ends: every sample of the episode's clock map,
one entry each, `"mono_ns utc_ns uncertainty_ns"` under its
zero-padded position, so receive times can be mapped to UTC exactly as
they were.

## Attachments

Written when recording starts, before the first message: every file of
the robot package the streams were declared in, exactly as it was when
capture loaded it, named after its path in the package (`package.toml`,
`urdf/arm7.urdf`), with its media type (`application/toml`,
`application/xml`, …). Meshes, and the textures and buffers they load,
are left out unless `capture.attach_meshes` is on, since a real
robot's take tens of megabytes per episode: they are files ending in
`.bin`, `.bmp`, `.dae`, `.glb`, `.gltf`, `.jpeg`, `.jpg`, `.ktx2`, `.mtl`, `.obj`, `.ply`, `.png`, `.stl`, `.tga`, `.webp`. An `unchecked` recording,
whose streams no package declares, carries the stream declarations it
was recorded from, under their file name.
